content:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH error rate on inference-api-prod (error_rate > 5% for 3m). Triggered 1891234567. @maya you're oncall.

maya (oncall): Ack. I'm seeing 5xx spikes across r1/r2. Looking at pods. No obvious deploys from deploy-bot.

alex (sre): Joining. Seen this on canary earlier but lower magnitude. Any customer-impact ETA?

maya (oncall): Initial customer impact: request failures ~4% of traffic, tail latency degrading. Flagging product for visibility @sam.

sam (product): Thanks. Which endpoints? Chat generation and /batch-embed seem affected. A few customers on Dedicated reported errors.

kim (eng-runtime): Looking at the runtime logs. KV cache warming failing intermittently, OOM retries on some GPUs. Pushing a quick scale w/ extra capacity to warm cache.

luis (ops): Scaling now: bumping pool inference-prod-g1 by +2 nodes. Applying temporary traffic-shed to non-critical routes.

incident-bot: Action log: scaleup requested by luis at 1891234620.

maya (oncall): While scale finishes, I'm going to silence noisy downstream alerts to reduce pager noise so oncall can focus. Will silence alerts with tag:inference:non-customer for 30m.

alex (sre): Agreed. The alert storm is masking the real signal. Quick note: DO NOT silence the core request-error-rate monitor. Only silencing auxiliary monitors.

maya (oncall): Executing silence: 
```bash
# datadog mute command (placeholder)
ddctl mute --scope "team:devex" --duration 30m --reason "incident mitigation: reduce noise"
```

observability-bot: Mute applied to 12 monitors: monitors/12345, monitors/12346... (audit id 9f8a).

kim (eng-runtime): Scale completed at 1891234702. Pods are coming up. I'm warming KV caches with synthetic traffic: 5k requests to /warm-cache.

maya (oncall): Post-scale status: error_rate dropped to ~1.2% and tail lat 95p reduced from 1.2s -> 650ms. Still want to tune thresholds to avoid repeats.

sam (product): Good to hear. Can we confirm no ongoing customer retries or saga effects? I'll ping CS.

luis (ops): Created maintenance window in Monitoring: 1891234800 - 1891236600 (30m buffer). This prevents repeated noisy pages while we validate.

alex (sre): Note for post-incident: current threshold for alert `inference_api_error_rate` is 2% over 5m. That was too sensitive during transient scale events. Propose: change to 4% over 5m with a secondary check that ties to sustained control-plane errors.

kim (eng-runtime): Also found that autoscaler cooldown is 60s which caused oscillation. Recommend increase cooldown to 180s for this pool.

maya (oncall): I'll open a quick follow-up ticket with proposed threshold and cooldown changes and assign to observability + runtime. Ticket: https://issues.redwood.internal/INC-4521

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial. Root cause: resource pressure + cache warm path regression.

sam (product): Customer comms: CS to send proactive note to impacted Dedicated customers. No widespread outage.

alex (sre): After we close this, we should run a load-replay against the new thresholds. Observability, can you create a dashboard that compares error_rate vs scale events vs cooldown windows?

observability-bot: Created dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/6a1b/incident-noise-sweep (panels: error_rate, scale_events, tail_latency, autoscaler_actions). Please review.

luis (ops): Quick checklist before closing: 
- remove temporary mute (or let it expire)
- validate maintenance window scheduled for 1h (can shorten)
- apply autoscaler cooldown change in staging then prod

maya (oncall): I'll keep oncall until next handoff in 15m. If metrics stay stable I'll mark incident resolved and start the post-incident cleanup doc.

kim (eng-runtime): Pushed autoscaler cooldown change to staging config. Runbook snippet we used: 
```yaml
autoscaler:
  cooldown_seconds: 180
  scale_up_step: 2
  scale_down_step: 1
```

alex (sre): After action: we'll schedule a noise-pruning session to sweep alerts that fire during expected scale events (e.g., pre-warm). Could add suppression rules rather than pure silence.

maya (oncall): Status update at 1891235030: metrics stable for 8m, error_rate at 0.9%. I'm removing myself from hot-rotation, will update the incident channel with post-incident action items.

sam (product): Thanks all. Please include the list of monitors we muted in the post-incident so we can evaluate whether to convert them to 'suppressed during scale' rules.

luis (ops): I'll keep the maintenance window open for another 20m then close it if stable.

kim (eng-runtime): Filing the follow-ups now: INC-4521 (threshold + cooldown), INC-4522 (dashboard + validation), INC-4523 (suppression rules).

alex (sre): For validation step: run the existing workload-replay job with 2x traffic for 30m and confirm no repeat of alert storm, then record thresholds in monitoring repo.

observability-bot: Noted. I will add a checklist item to link the load-replay results into the dashboard.

maya (oncall): Closing note: good collaboration. Lessons: prefer suppression rules for expected operational bursts vs blanket silences; ensure autoscaler cooldown aligns with cache-warm semantics.

incident-bot: Incident resolved at 1891235600 (mitigation verified). Follow-ups created: INC-4521, INC-4522, INC-4523.
